Guides / 06—08

Plan repeat patterns and print direction

Printed fabric can require more length than a plain-fabric layout suggests.

Vijeron · Updated 9 October 2026

Measure a repeat

Measure from one motif point to its identical next point along the fabric length. Record motif placement against each panel's cut edge. If the print has an up and down, align all panels one way even when alternating direction would use less fabric.

Test with a scaled sketch

Draw usable fabric width and rectangles at cut size. Mark each row's motif start. Move rows when prints must match at a seam, then measure the extra length. The panel calculator provides simple repeat-rectangle arithmetic, not print-matching simulation.

Keep the print measurement

At purchase, record the measured repeat, direction and extra length you actually decided on. When repeat information is unavailable, avoid an invented universal margin. Ask for a sample or measure the bolt and redo the plan before a large purchase.

Worked example

Two rows of 52 cm panels give 104 cm base length. If a scaled print plan adds 14 cm, enter 14 cm extra for a total of 118 cm.

Pitfall to avoid

Do not present one extra percentage as correct for every print; designs and orientations differ.
